title: Adaptive proxy windowing and tool-call rate smoothing
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Several customers reported intermittent function/tool-calling failures and long tail latency when clients opened many concurrent streaming connections. Root cause analysis showed that the gateway's fixed per-connection proxy buffer window caused head-of-line backpressure and aggressive route-level payload enforcement caused sudden request drops under bursty tool-call fanout. This PR introduces an adaptive proxy windowing algorithm plus a token-rate smoothing layer for OpenAI-compat function/tool calls to reduce transient failures while keeping route payload limits enforced.

Summary of approach: 1) Adaptive proxy windowing: replace the static per-connection buffer with a sliding window that tracks recent token-forward throughput and dynamically adjusts the in-memory buffer and flush thresholds. The window is conservative for low-throughput connections (to minimize memory) and expands under sustained streaming to reduce fragmentation. 2) Tool-call rate smoothing: introduce a lightweight leaky-bucket per-route that smooths bursts of downstream tool/function calls originating from a single incoming request (helps when a single response triggers many parallel webhook/tool calls). 3) Graceful payload enforcement: move strict payload-size enforcement to a two-step check: a fast soft quota that allows short-lived overshoots (logged and meter-tagged) and a stricter hard quota which only triggers if the overshoot persists beyond a configurable time window. 4) OpenAI-compat shim updates: the compatibility layer now maps function-calling handshakes to the new smoothing API and translates the gateway's streaming frames into a stable JSONL framing when needed to avoid client-side parser errors. 5) Observability and experiments: new metrics, traces, and an A/B rollout to validate behavior under production traffic.

Key outcomes from internal canary (1 week, mixed traffic): - 95th percentile streaming latency reduced by ~18% for endpoints with heavy tool-call fanout. - Tool/function-call transient failures decreased by ~42% in end-to-end regression tests. - Memory usage per proxy worker increased by ~6% under steady-state high-concurrency workloads; we added a configurable hard cap.

Compatibility notes: The default behavior is opt-in via route flag "adaptive_proxy_window": true for routes. For OpenAI-compat routes we enable smoothing by default but keep a feature flag (compat_tool_smoothing) to toggle to previous behavior for quick rollback. No API contract changes for customers; the updates are internal gateway optimizations but can affect behavior at the margins (short-lived overshoot vs immediate 413 responses).

Testing and QA: - Unit and integration tests for window sizing heuristics and bucket refill semantics. - Added e2e scenario simulating a single chat response causing 40 parallel tool calls; validated rate smoothing and end-to-end correctness (function-call responses are aggregated into the stream without reordering). - Load testing showing improved 95p latency when aggregated across routes with high function-call density. - CI initially failed a flakey test (proxy window race) and was fixed by adding an ordering assertion and a deterministic timer in test harness.

Rollback and rollout plan: Gradual rollout over 3 days: 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic for routes with the feature flag enabled. Automated canary checks validate error rate, 95p latency, and the new metric "proxy_window_fill_ratio". Fast rollback toggles the route flag to false and reverts to the previous stable windowing implementation.

Notes on operational tuning: - Default soft overshoot window: 200ms; hard quota enforcement: 5s. - Default per-route smoothing token refill: 50 tokens/sec with burst of 200 tokens. - New admin endpoints expose per-route buckets and current window sizes for debugging.

Related work and references: This PR builds on ENG-4921 (gateway buffering investigation) and ENG-4987 (fncall meltdown post-traffic spike). Related docs: updated compat docs and gateway operational runbook.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we make the soft overshoot window configurable per-tenant? I worry enterprise customers will want tighter controls.
Maya Patel (reply): Added per-tenant override in the config; default continues to be route-level. See gateway/config/proxy_buffering.yaml.
Ravi Singh: The JSONL framing change is subtle for some older clients — did we add integration tests for legacy parsers?

Maya Patel (reply): Yes, added sdk/ts/tests/openai_compat_streaming.test.ts which exercises both legacy newline-delimited parsing and the JSONL frames. Also kept the old framing available behind a flag.
Sofia Martinez: CI was failing due to a race in the test harness; confirmed fix and reran CI. Approving after green builds.

release_notes:
- Introduced adaptive proxy windowing to reduce head-of-line streaming latency; opt-in per-route flag.
- Added tool/function-call rate smoothing to reduce transient failures under high fanout.
- OpenAI-compat layer maps function-calling handshakes to the smoothing API and optionally uses stable JSONL framing to avoid parser errors.
- New observability metrics: proxy_window_fill_ratio, toolcall_smoothing_rate, proxy_buffer_overshoot_count.
short_description: Adaptive proxy buffering and rate-smoothing to improve streaming stability and fncall reliability under bursty workloads.
notes_for_release_manager: Enable feature flag on a subset of routes first. Monitor proxy_window_fill_ratio, error rate, and 95p streaming latency. Be ready to toggle compat_tool_smoothing off if client incompatibilities observed.
